sources_quoted.quote: Ability recasts are scheduled on **one shared timeline** (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed *and* no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it *starts* within the window (`_schedule_shared_casts`). With `c_i` the effective cooldown of ability `i`, the cast epochs of a solo ability are `0, c_i, 2c_i, ...` -- again a deterministic renewal schedule; the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order.

independent_computation.step_1_scenario_reading: The scenario id decomposes as champion=Syndra, option=custom cast order, value=120. 120 is Syndra's signature option value in the cached audit data: the splinters option runs 0-120, 120 is its maximum and the +15% total-AP capstone. The corpus setup vocabulary (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json) confirms `champion_options` is a real per-scenario setup key. Reading 120 as ability haste or as a fight duration cannot explain a change in a cast ORDINAL at all (see step 5), while reading it as splinters=120 does.
independent_computation.step_2_castable_slots: At splinters >= 40 Dark Sphere becomes a stocked-charge (ammo) ability with a second charge, which the Syndra module exposes as its own SLOTS key `Q2` ("synthetic Q2 (2nd charge)", "40+ Q charges via Q2 slot"). The wiki ammo atom independently confirms Syndra's Dark Sphere is a stocked-cast ability. Hence at splinters=120 the champion has FIVE castable slots: Q, Q2, W, E, R (P is a passive buff, not a cast).
independent_computation.step_3_opening_schedule: Apply the shared-timeline rule quoted from math-foundations 1.1. Every slot is off cooldown at t=0 (both Q charges are stocked at fight start), so mutual exclusion is the only constraint and the five first casts are laid down back-to-back, greedily in the user's custom order. Sourced cast times: Q 'none'=0, Q2=Q=0, W 'none'=0, E 0.25, R 0.25 => the five opening casts occupy 0 + 0 + 0 + 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.50 s total.
independent_computation.step_4_no_recast_can_intervene: The earliest possible recast is at min_i c_i. From data/champions.json with cd' = cd*100/(100+AH): W rank 5 = 8 s -> 3.64 s at AH 120, 2.67 s even at an unreachable AH 200; Q = 7 s (cache marks it affectedByCdr=false; 3.18 s at AH 120 if haste were applied); E = 15 s -> 6.82 s at AH 120; R is single-cast per the documented model constraint. Every one of these is >> 0.50 s, so no recast can be scheduled before the fifth first cast. Therefore cast_timeline entries [0..4] are exactly the five slots' FIRST casts, in the scenario's custom order.
independent_computation.step_5_leaf_value: cast_timeline[4] is the first cast of the fifth slot in the custom order, so its per-slot ordinal is 1. NEW VALUE = 1 is correct. The old value 2 requires a re-cast to occupy the 5th timeline position, which by step 4 can only happen when only FOUR castable slots exist -- i.e. when the 40+-splinter second Dark Sphere charge is missing from the shared timeline. That contradicts the splinters=120 setup and the module's own Q2 slot, so 2 is the pre-fix (four-slot) value.

assumptions_and_residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition itself lives in scripts/ (golden_snapshot.py) and tests/, which this oracle is forbidden to read; the setup was reconstructed from the scenario id plus the cached audit data. The identification 120 = splinters (max) is inference, though it is the only reading under which an ordinal at index 4 can legitimately change at all.

If `ordinal` were counted per ability LETTER rather than per cast SLOT, the Q2 entry would read as Q's 2nd cast (ordinal 2) and the value at index 4 would depend on where Q2 sits in the custom order. The module's SLOTS key is `Q2`, a first-class slot, so a per-slot count (=1 for its first cast) is the consistent reading; a per-letter count would also make the ordinal field ambiguous for any entry labelled Q2.

Independent of that labelling question, a 4-slot timeline can never produce ordinal 1 at index 4 and a 5-slot timeline can never produce ordinal 2 there via a recast; the verdict therefore rests on Syndra having five castable slots at splinters=120, which the cached audit data states directly.
